trials.name: roll-augmented input
trials.hypothesis: The observed target is shifted cyclically by X/2 along x. Concatenating the observation with a copy shifted back by X//2 (only slicing and concatenation) lets the 1x1 stem line up target and build at every cell. The recipe also gives about 80 updates instead of 32. If success stays near 0 and the agent still presses DONE first, then either the shift is not the problem or the build/missing channels are shifted too.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def roll_x(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., s:], t[..., :s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        xin = torch.cat([obs, roll_x(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(xin)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

Learned Linear layers that mix along the X axis and along the Y axis are applied to projected stem features, and their outputs are concatenated with the local features. import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
MIXC = 24
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.px = nn.Conv2d(COL, MIXC, 1)
        self.xmix = nn.Linear(int(spec.X), int(spec.X))
        self.py = nn.Conv2d(COL, MIXC, 1)
        self.ymix = nn.Linear(int(spec.Y), int(spec.Y))
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL + 2 * MIXC, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        mx = self.xmix(self.px(s))
        my = self.ymix(self.py(s).transpose(2, 3)).transpose(2, 3)
        h = torch.cat([s, mx, my], dim=1)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(h))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"lr": 0.002, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def roll_x(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., s:], t[..., :s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        xin = torch.cat([obs, roll_x(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(xin)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., s:], t[..., :s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2

            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH + COL, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        xin = torch.cat([obs, roll_x(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 2, "gae_lambda": 0.95}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


def roll_x(t, s):
    if s <= 0:
        return t
    return torch.cat([t[..., s:], t[..., :s]], dim=-1)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

        super().__init__()
        self.shift = int(spec.X) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        xin = torch.cat([obs, roll_x(obs, self.shift)], dim=1)

- dev behaviour: placements per episode 10.77; episodes ending with DONE before any placement 0.0%; mean IoU 0.983; cells placed inside / outside the target per episode 24.31 / 0.49

analyses.1: The starting network scored 0 on both seeds. It learned to press DONE straight away (episode length went from 1.7 to 1.0, with 100% DONE before any placement). The traces suggest why. The target column heights the agent observes are the real design shifted cyclically by 4 columns (X/2) along x, with no shift along y. This holds on both diagnostic designs: design row 1 is 00220000 and the observed row is 00000022. The build channels match the actions, so they are not shifted. A network that only looks a few cells around each position can never line up the target with the build, so every placement looks like a loss and DONE wins. The first fix is to realign the input: concatenate the observation with a copy shifted by X//2, or let the network learn to mix information across rows and columns. I also want more PPO updates, since the default gives only 32. No noise estimate exists yet.
analyses.2: The observed target is rolled cyclically by X/2 along x. You can see this in the traces: target column 6 shows up at column 2. Only r1c1, which concatenates a copy rolled back by X/2, learned anything, and both its seeds were high (0.86 and 0.92). Every other run settled on pressing DONE first, because random placements earn negative reward and DONE earns 0. r1c3 kept the roll but collapsed on both seeds. It changed several things at once (2 epochs, 64 envs, entropy 0.02, lambda 0.95, a dilated layer), so we can't tell which one hurt. r1c1's training success was still rising at the end (0.73 at 75%, 0.81 at 100%), so the run is probably short of samples or updates. Its dev IoU is 0.974 and it places about 0.7 cells outside the target per episode, so the remaining misses are small errors, not alignment failures. This round makes single changes to r1c1: (1) 2 epochs, which gives about 1.4x the samples; (2) a learning rate of 0.002; (3) feeding all X cyclic x-shifts so the network learns which shift to use. That last one would carry over to worlds whose offset we don't know.
analyses.3: The observed target is shifted cyclically by X/2 along x. The design and observed height maps in the traces show this exactly. Adding a copy rolled back by X/2 is the change that made the agent work: without it, every run (r1c2 and the starting architecture) learned to press DONE first. The best trial is r2c1 (2 PPO epochs, 128 environments) at 0.937, against 0.888 with 3 epochs. Both seeds improved, so the gain from more fresh samples is probably real. Raising lr to 0.002 gave 0.894 against 0.888, which is noise. Feeding in all x-shifts (r2c2) was unstable: one seed scored 0.08. r1c3 collapsed to DONE, but it changed several things at once (64 environments, entropy 0.02, gae_lambda 0.95, a dilated layer), so no single cause can be named. The remaining failures are small: mean IoU 0.987 and about 0.4 cells placed outside the target per episode. They are likely wrong ordering under overhangs or unneeded extra bricks. Next I test 1 PPO epoch (more samples), gamma 0.99 (more credit for the end-of-episode exact-build bonus), and a skip that feeds the stem's per-cell features straight into the footprint head.
analyses.4: The observed target is shifted cyclically by X/2. Undoing that shift is the only architecture change that worked: every run with it either reached about 0.85–0.94 dev success or fell to near 0 by seed luck. Fewer PPO epochs helped. 3 epochs gave 0.888 and 2 epochs gave 0.937, the best so far (r2c1). With 1 epoch the agent used only 1x1 bricks, which cannot form overhangs, and scored 0.077. Doubling the learning rate at 3 epochs gave about 0.89, the same as before. Adding the stem features to the footprint head (0.907) was within noise of the best. The main risk is that one seed collapses, either to pressing DONE or to the 1x1-only habit, as with gamma 0.99 and with all x-shifts as input. At 2 epochs r2c1's training success was still rising at the end (0.894 to 0.926), so the agent has not finished learning. Because this is the last round, all three candidates keep r2c1's network and change one recipe setting each.
